Subject: Post-call: Data handling and VPC deployment follow-up (PII, retention, egress)

Hi Alicia —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery so everyone has a single source of truth. I’ve cc'd Michael per the call.

Recap (from our call):
- Use case: customer support automation + sensitive customer identifiers in prompts (account numbers, partial SSNs)
- Desired deployment: Private/VPC in us-east-1 with no public egress for production workloads
- Compliance asks: PII handling controls, retention policy, audit logs forwarded to customer logging, SOC 2 evidence
- Procurement timeline: security clearances + legal reviews expected over 4–6 weeks

Open questions we promised to follow up on:
1) Exact retention window you need for user-level logs & model inputs/outputs (you mentioned ~90 days yesterday — can you confirm)
2) Are you able to accept a control plane managed by Redwood that communicates over a private peering, or do you need fully customer-hosted control plane (air-gapped/on-prem)?
3) Any mandatory egress constraints (e.g., absolutely no outbound internet for inference nodes)?
4) KMS/HSM preference for at-rest encryption (BYOK vs Redwood-managed)

Attachments: rw-dataflow-v1.png (data flow diagram), priv-vpc-svc-sheet.pdf (private deployment service overview). I’ve also added links to our compliance docs in the attached service sheet.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm retention & egress constraints and whether an on-prem/air-gapped option is required for production (reply to this thread)
- We loop in our Security/SE (Dev and Ethan) to propose an architecture that meets the constraints and return a checklist 
- Align on a 60-min follow-up next week to walk the architecture and procurement ask

Thanks — I’ll coordinate times after your reply.

Best,

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@fintrust.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: Data handling and VPC deployment follow-up (PII, retention, egress)

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing the attachments and talking with security: 

1) Retention: we require model inputs/outputs and audit logs retained for 90 days by default. For any data classified as PII we require automatic redaction where possible and deletion after 90 days unless explicitly retained by a legal hold.

2) Data residency: production must be in us-east-1. We cannot allow copy/replication to any other region without prior approval.

3) Egress: production inference nodes must not have general internet egress. Outbound connections are permitted only to the customer logging endpoint (ELK) over a private peering or transit gateway; metadata-only health checks to Redwood control plane are negotiable but need to be scoped (IP allowlist).

4) Control plane: preference is customer-managed control plane in our VPC if feasible. If Redwood-managed control plane is required, it must connect over a dedicated private peering with mutual TLS and IP allowlist. For one of our high-sensitivity environments we will likely require an air-gapped/on-prem variant.

5) Encryption: at-rest using our KMS (BYOK) where possible. We also need proof of HSM usage for key protection for the highest-sensitivity environment.

6) Logging: we will need detailed audit logs (request id, timestamp, requestor id, tokenized input indicator) forwarded to our syslog/ELK cluster. Logs should not contain raw PII (tokenization/redaction rules are necessary).

I’ve attached the FinTrust security questionnaire (FinTrust_Security_Questions.xlsx) with a few high-priority items filled. Procurement and InfoSec expect answers to sections 2–6 before we move to an NDA/POC. Our procurement lead (Michael O'Neill) will also be copied on the follow-up.

Can your engineers respond to the technical items (control plane options, egress pattern, BYOK/HSM support, redaction strategy, and on-prem air-gapped process)? We’re available for a technical deep-dive Thurs 3/5 or Fri 3/6 (Eastern).

Regards,
Alicia Gomez
Head of Cloud Security | FinTrust Bank

From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-call: Data handling and VPC deployment follow-up (PII, retention, egress)

Hi Alicia — looping in technical details and options. Thanks for the clear asks — below is a concise proposal and some questions where we need more specifics to finalize the architecture and checklist.

Short answer summary: Redwood can support the requirements. Options (ordered by how close they map to your asks):

Option A — Customer-hosted inference + customer control plane (recommended)- Inference runtime runs in your AWS account (us-east-1) inside private subnets (no public IPs).
- Model artifacts and runtime images sourced from Redwood but delivered as signed, versioned artifacts stored in customer S3 (or transferred via offline medium for air-gapped).
- No default internet egress from inference nodes; outbound traffic limited to your ELK endpoint and (optionally) our control plane IPs over private peering.
- At-rest encryption using customer KMS (BYOK) for model cache & logs.
- Audit logs forwarded to your logging endpoint via VPC peering/Transit Gateway (we ship a small forwarder sidecar that pushes logs over an mTLS connection to your collector).

Option B — Hybrid: Redwood-managed control plane + customer-hosted inference nodes- Control plane communicates over private peering. Minimal metadata (job id, health checks) flows to control plane; no raw prompts or PII leave your VPC.
- Same KMS/BYOK setup as Option A.

Option C — On-prem/air-gapped- We provide container images and signed artifacts; deployment is offline via transferred artifacts (S3 export or physical media) and validated checksums.
- Support for a completely air-gapped inference env where outbound connections are restricted. Periodic offline model updates and a local logging sink that you provide.

Key technical notes and commitments:
- Encryption in transit: mTLS between all components. If we peer, we’ll also require IP allowlisting.
- KV cache & runtime artifacts: ephemeral and encrypted; persistent logs go to your ELK only.
- Redaction: we provide a configurable input sanitizer that can run as a pre-processing sidecar to remove/replace PII before it reaches the model. We will work with your team to codify tokenization/redaction rules (regex-based + configurable PII classifiers).
- KMS/HSM: BYOK is supported. For HSM attestations we can integrate with customer HSMs or provide evidence of Redwood’s HSM usage for control-plane secrets. For the highest-sensitivity env we recommend customer-managed HSMs (FIPS 140-2/3 compliant).

Questions for you (so we can finalize the checklist):
1) Expected steady-state QPS and peak concurrent requests for production (per region)?
2) Are embeddings stored/queried server-side? If yes, do embeddings contain PII that must be redacted/encrypted separately?
3) Which exact ELK endpoint hostnames/IPs should we allowlist for the log forwarder?
4) For the air-gapped env: do you prefer artifact transfer via signed S3 export or physical media?

Attachments: updated dataflow diagram (rw-dataflow-v1.png) and a draft deployment checklist (priv-vpc-svc-sheet.pdf). I’ve annotated the diagram with the two deployment options.

If helpful, we can run a 45–60 min technical call to walk the diagram and answer the questionnaire items. I’m available Thur 3/5 between 10:00–14:00 ET and Fri 3/6 09:00–12:00 ET.

Thanks,
